metadata.name: Red Forty
metadata.author: Pedaleira
metadata.summary: A classic-voiced high gain preamp with a big low end (a 12AX7 input stage, a gain pot, three cascaded gain stages, a treble-middle-bass tone stack) into a push-pull EL34 power amp with a strong resonance (depth) control. The topology and the starting values are those of the High Gain description; the gain law, the levels, the clipping points, the tone stack and the feedback network were then fitted to measurements of a reference amp (its GAIN sweep, its line-level responses and its tone, presence and resonance sweeps). The gain is staged so that playing level leaves the input stage clean: the first grid sees a guitar-like level, the gain it gave up sits in the divider before the last stage, and a bleed capacitor across the 470k before the third stage lifts the highs into the clipping (fitted to the DI run v26). Every value the fit moved is marked "fitted" with what it was fitted to.
references: D. T. Yeh and J. O. Smith, Discretization of the '59 Fender Bassman Tone Stack, DAFx-06, 2006
J. Pakarinen and D. T. Yeh, A review of digital techniques for modeling vacuum-tube guitar amplifiers, Computer Music Journal 33(2), 2009
Pedaleira measurements of a reference amp played through a modelling unit's USB input: GAIN sweeps with a 1 kHz staircase, THD at -54 dBFS, the test signal's sweeps at -18 dBFS (2026)
